fluff.overview:
The Adder is a light Clan OmniMech first produced in 3010 by Clan Star Adder in preparation for the anticipated invasion of the Inner Sphere. Designated "Puma" by Inner Sphere forces who first engaged it during the Clan Invasion, the Adder was designed to match or exceed the firepower and survivability of the medium BattleMechs that Wolf's Dragoons reported as most common among Successor State armies. This ambitious design philosophy resulted in a 35-ton chassis capable of challenging 'Mechs nearly twice its weight.

One of the most widely produced Clan light OmniMechs, the Adder serves primarily as a fire-support platform, though its versatile OmniMech pod system has spawned numerous configurations suited to roles ranging from anti-infantry work to electronic warfare. Clan Star Adder originally produced the design at their own facilities, though manufacturing has since spread well beyond their control.
fluff.capabilities:
The Adder maximizes available payload through aggressive weight-saving measures. A Hooded Endo-Lite endo steel chassis and Great Father 210 Extra-Light engine combine to free nearly half the 'Mech's total mass for weapons and equipment, resulting in an impressive sixteen tons of pod space. The chassis mounts six tons of Star Lite ferro-fibrous armor, providing protection comparable to many medium 'Mechs while maintaining a top speed of 97 kilometers per hour. A single DuPont Ultra PM flamer is fixed in the head mount across all configurations, a peculiarity that speaks to the Star Adders' original anti-infantry doctrine.

The Primary configuration exemplifies the Adder's design philosophy with twin extended-range particle projector cannons linked to an advanced targeting computer, enabling precise long-range fire that can threaten far heavier opponents. However, this fearsome armament generates considerable heat, requiring disciplined fire management. The Trueborn Ultra 945B communications system and Adder Special V8.6 targeting-tracking suite provide the electronic backbone for all configurations, ensuring reliable battlefield coordination regardless of the weapons payload selected.

The chassis does suffer from relatively thin side torso armor, making the Adder vulnerable to flanking attacks. Pilots quickly learn that the design rewards standoff engagement over close-quarters brawling, and most configurations reflect this reality with long-range weapon systems.
fluff.history:
The Adder's development was intrinsically linked to Clan Star Adder's preparations for the eventual invasion of the Inner Sphere. When Wolf's Dragoons delivered their reconnaissance reports on Inner Sphere military capabilities, the Star Adders recognized an opportunity to create a training opponent that could accurately simulate Successor State opposition. The resulting reorganization of Kappa Galaxy into an Inner Sphere-emulating force drove the need for an OmniMech that could replicate common medium 'Mech loadouts while demonstrating clear Clan technological superiority.

Several of the Adder's primary configurations, including the B, C, and D variants, were designed specifically based on Wolf's Dragoons intelligence to mirror the weapon combinations most frequently encountered among House armies. Kappa Galaxy received priority allocation of these configurations, using them to provide realistic opposition training for other Star Adder units. The irony that the Adder would eventually fight alongside Inner Sphere forces rather than against them was not lost on Clan historians.

Despite the Star Adders' attempts to restrict access to their signature light OmniMech, the design's effectiveness made it a prize in Trials of Possession. By 3045, the Adder had proliferated throughout Clan space, produced by facilities far beyond Star Adder control. The Clan Invasion brought the design into direct contact with the Inner Sphere forces it had been created to fight, and the Puma designation entered common usage among House militaries.

Following the establishment of Clan Wolf-in-Exile on Arc-Royal, the Adder became one of the first Clan OmniMechs produced within the Inner Sphere when Assault Tech Industries on Donegal began manufacturing after the success of their Jaguar line. The Exiled Wolves retained most production for their own touman but also exported the base chassis to Inner Sphere buyers under its Spheroid designation. This commercial success represented a final irony for the Star Adders: their signature 'Mech, designed to conquer the Inner Sphere, had instead been welcomed as a valued commodity by the very powers it was meant to subjugate.

A notable rivalry developed between Adder and Cougar pilots following the latter 'Mech's introduction in the 3050s, with aggressive Jade Falcon Cougar pilots frequently seeking out Adders to prove the superiority of their newer design. This competition reached particular intensity during Khan Malvina Hazen's campaign to take Tharkad, where numerous Adder versus Cougar duels played out on the Tatyana Islands between Falcon forces and the Second Royal Guards' Lyran-operated Pumas.
fluff.deployment: The L configuration adds jump capability to the Adder chassis for the first time. Six jump jets enable 180-meter jumps, dramatically improving tactical mobility on rough terrain. Four Streak LRM-5 launchers ensure every launched missile finds its target, while paired extended-range medium lasers provide backup firepower. An ECM suite disrupts enemy targeting and communications. Introduced in 3147, this configuration stands as a significant evolution of the Adder concept, trading raw firepower for battlefield mobility and electronic warfare capability. The L configuration has proven particularly effective in reconnaissance and raiding operations where its combination of speed, jump capability, and ECM allows it to operate where other Adders cannot.
